summary: Privileged Network Ops: Temporary cross-cloud service account delegation & identity boundary review
description:
Issue summary:
Network & SRE requested temporary cross-cloud delegation so Privileged Network Ops can execute a live debug of a networking path impacting model shard replication. The goal is to grant short-lived access across both AWS and GCP accounts without creating long-lived keys or broad service accounts.

Impact:
- Ongoing replication lag observed for shard mapping in prod us-east; incident window non-critical but blocking a cross-region failover drill.
- Requires engineers from Network Ops to run packet captures and inspect IAM-authenticated calls that traverse AWS VPC peering and a GCP VPC-SC perimeter.

Background / Constraints:
- Security policy forbids long-lived service account keys and cross-account IAM roles without an approved boundary review.
- GCP project is inside an organization-wide VPC Service Controls perimeter for prod resources.
- AWS landing accounts have SCPs that prevent AssumeRole from outside the organization except via approved OIDC brokers.
- On-prem management tooling references both cloud provider identities; we must avoid exporting credentials to local machines.

Request / Proposed change:
1) Provision a scoped, time-limited delegation that allows Network Ops to impersonate a read-only service identity in both clouds for 4 hours.
2) Implement conditional role bindings tied to source IP ranges (Redwood-managed jump hosts) and MFA session presence.
3) Avoid creating long-lived keys; use short-lived credentials via our internal JIT-broker (auth-broker.redwood) and confirm audit logging to KMS/Audit.
4) Security review: run an identity boundary checklist and get explicit approval from Security and Cloud Infra in this ticket.

Acceptance criteria:
- Network Ops can run targeted diagnostics for up to 4 hours without manual intervention.
- No long-lived keys were created; all actions are logged to central audit and visible in the Security dashboard.
- Boundaries prevent lateral movement beyond the scoped read-only roles.

Timeline:
- Need delegation window scheduled: 2026-03-04 10:00 - 14:00 UTC (tentative).
comments: 2026-03-01 — Diego Alvarez: Scoped role bindings drafted. Waiting for Security to validate conditional IAM statement for GCP impersonation (needs VPC-SC compatibility).

2026-03-02 — Priya Singh (Security): Quick check: we must not allow iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy on prod SA. Will propose an alternative binding that removes policy editing and restricts 'iam.serviceAccounts.actAs' only from the broker service account.
2026-03-03 — Maya Chen: Confirming Network Ops available on 2026-03-04. Please include runbook links and monitoring hooks in the implementation so we can revoke early if needed.
2026-03-05 — Diego Alvarez: Implemented delegated role in staging; rolling the same pattern to prod requires org-policy exception. Opening org-policy ticket with Cloud Infra.
2026-03-06 — Cloud Infra (Evan Park): Org-policy exception granted for the explicit principal and timeframe. Please proceed with JIT broker configuration and run the scheduled debug.
investigation_notes: Checked IAM bindings in AWS prod account: existing role 'redwood-network-debugger' exists but trust policy restricts to internal services only, not external OIDC. SCP prevents external principals. Command used: aws iam get-role --role-name redwood-network-debugger

GCP: service account 'sa-net-debug@prod.gcp' has 'roles/iam.serviceAccountUser' assigned to group 'ops-net-dev' but VPC-SC blocks access from outside the perimeter. Console evidence: 'Request blocked by VPC-SC' in cloudaudit logs.

Hypothesis: Primary blocker is identity boundary enforcement (org policies + VPC-SC + AWS SCPs). Short-lived JIT via auth-broker should work once brokers are added to allowlist and conditional bindings restrict sources.
Test in staging: created ephemeral principal via auth-broker, validated impersonation for 'sa-net-debug' for 30 minutes. Observed audit entries in staging audit log with 'auth_broker:session_id' tag.
Found a dependent constraint: On AWS, SSO issuer is not currently included in the target account's AssumeRole trust policy. Will add SSO oidc:sub mapping for the broker after security approval.
Logs referenced: https://logs.redwood.internal/queries/replication_lag_2026-02-27 and cloudaudit-prod GCP entries ID: CA-20260227-17:23:02
resolution: Partial workaround implemented: Staging JIT flow validated; org-policy exception granted for the requested principal and timeframe. On 2026-03-04, Network Ops executed the debug window using the JIT-broker; replication checks completed and no sensitive policy changes were made. Follow-ups: 1) Formalize JIT runbook and add automated revocation steps (task assigned to Cloud Infra). 2) Security to run a post-access audit and sign-off. 3) Replace manual org-policy exception with automated allowlist for the broker (tracked in linked issue INT-48001).
